t_e7cdb07ae9ca.prompt: Which steps create a script asset and attach it to a GameObject in this Unity version?

choices.text: Choose Assets > Create > MonoBehaviour Script, then add it to the GameObject in the Inspector.
Choose GameObject > 3D Object > Cube, then add a script from the Console.
Choose Window > General > Console, then drag the Console onto the GameObject.
Choose Component > Physics > Rigidbody, then rename the Rigidbody as a script.

t_e7cdb07ae9ca.explanation: A MonoBehaviour Script is created from Assets > Create. You can attach it by dragging it onto the GameObject or by using Add Component in the Inspector. The other options create or open something else. See “Create the Spinner script and attach it to a cube.”

t_6d124d690929.prompt: A script starts with `public float speed = 75f;`. After the component has been attached, the Inspector shows Speed as 125. What speed does the script use when you press Play?

choices.text: 75, because the value in the script always takes priority.
75, because Unity averages the two values.
125, because the Inspector keeps the component’s value.
125, but only after you change the script and save it.

t_6d124d690929.explanation: Once the component exists, its Inspector value overrides the starting value in the code. The code’s value is used when the script is first attached or when you reset the component. The script value does not always take priority, and Unity does not average the values. See “Change variables to change behavior.”

t_37a6669f3643.prompt: Multiplying a rotation amount by `Time.deltaTime` helps a speed in degrees per second stay consistent on computers with different frame rates.

choices.text: True
False

t_37a6669f3643.explanation: `Time.deltaTime` accounts for how long the last frame took, so the rotation amount changes with frame time while the speed remains expressed per second. See “Write the code that spins the cube.”

t_c51a383d1e61.prompt: Several compiler errors appear in the Console after you edit a script. What should you do first?

choices.text: Fix the error with the largest line number, save the script, and check the Console again.
Fix the first error in the list, save the script, and check the Console again.
Delete the script, create another one, and copy the code back into it.
Press Play to see which error changes the Game view, then fix that one.

t_c51a383d1e61.explanation: One mistake can cause other errors, so start with the first error in the list. After fixing it, save and look again; some later errors may disappear. The line number alone does not tell you which error to fix first, and Play cannot run while compiler errors remain. See “Break the script and fix it from the Console.”

t_eb225d32ee74.prompt: You double-click a Console compiler error and the code editor opens at a line in the script. What should you do next to use that error to fix the script?
t_eb225d32ee74.answer: Read the error’s file, line and column, code, and short message. Check the pointed-to line and, if needed, the line above it. Fix the first error, save the script, then return to Unity and check the Console again.
t_eb225d32ee74.explanation: The Console message identifies the file and location, gives an error code, and summarizes the problem. Double-clicking helps you find the relevant code. Fix the first error, save, and check again. See “Break the script and fix it from the Console.”

t_2ddde245b086.title: Weekly builds: variables and Console debugging
t_2ddde245b086.prompt:
You are building on the script skills you practiced this week. This build contributes to Weekly builds, which counts for 40% of your course grade.

In your OrbCollector project, create a cube named ScriptStudy and attach Spinner. Extend the script with a public float named rollSpeed. Make the cube rotate around its vertical and depth axes, then choose your own Speed and Roll Speed values in the Inspector. Introduce a capitalization error in `gameObject.name`, use the Console to find it, and fix it. Save Arena. Explain your chosen speeds and how you found and fixed the error, and copy the first Console error line into your explanation, because the fixed script no longer shows it. Note any help you used, including AI tools.

Your instructor will judge the script behavior, your Console debugging, and your explanation and evidence. Upload a screenshot showing the cube, Spinner (Script) values and Console, plus a short screen recording showing the cube rotate when you press Play and stop. Use common image and video file types that work on Windows and Mac, and upload both to the LMS by Sunday night this week. The LMS grade is complete or incomplete. A complete submission has the screenshot, the recording and the explanation, and the recording shows ScriptStudy turning around both axes.
steps: In OrbCollector, create a cube named ScriptStudy. Set its Position to 8, 1, -8 and attach the Spinner script.

In Spinner.cs, add a public float named rollSpeed with a starting value of 45f. Change the Rotate call so Speed controls the vertical axis and rollSpeed controls the depth axis. In the Inspector, choose your own Speed and Roll Speed for ScriptStudy (for example 75 and 150), then press Play to check both turns. Every cube with Spinner now has a Roll Speed of 45; set it to 0 on Pickup_Test and Pickup_Test_B if you want them to turn as before.

Change `gameObject.name` in the Debug.Log line to `gameObject.Name`, save the script, and read the first Console error. Double-click the error, restore the correct spelling, save, and check that Play works again.

Save Arena. Capture a screenshot showing ScriptStudy, its Spinner (Script) values and the Console. Make a short screen recording showing the cube turning when you press Play and stop. Upload both files to the LMS by Sunday night this week, with your explanation and a note of any help you used.
t_2ddde245b086.answerKey:
1. A cube named ScriptStudy is at Position 8, 1, -8 and has Spinner attached.
2. Add `public float rollSpeed = 45f;` and use `transform.Rotate(0f, speed * Time.deltaTime, rollSpeed * Time.deltaTime);`. Speed and Roll Speed are the student’s own values, for example 75 and 150; both axes turn during Play.
3. The Console reports an error because GameObject has no `Name` member with that capitalization. Restore `gameObject.name`, save, and confirm the script compiles and runs.
4. The LMS submission contains a screenshot showing the cube, Spinner values and Console; a short recording showing the cube turning during Play and stopping; and an explanation of the chosen speeds, the error fix and any help used.

t_a2d63ad6692f.prompt: You want a push to continue while you hold Left Shift. Which check should you read each frame?

choices.text: `Keyboard.current.leftShiftKey.wasPressedThisFrame`
`Input.GetKey(KeyCode.LeftShift)`
`Keyboard.current.leftShiftKey.wasReleasedThisFrame`
`Keyboard.current.leftShiftKey.isPressed`

t_a2d63ad6692f.explanation: `isPressed` stays true while the key is held. `wasPressedThisFrame` is true only on the frame the key goes down. `Input.GetKey` uses the old Input class, which throws an error in this project. `wasReleasedThisFrame` detects a release, not a held key. Review “Read the keyboard with a new script” and “Challenges.”

t_dc7fcd2a8e0a.prompt: Which setup reads keyboard input and applies a Rigidbody push on the physics schedule?

choices.text: Read keys in `FixedUpdate`, save the direction, then call `AddForce` in `Update`.
Read keys in `LateUpdate`, then call `AddForce` in `LateUpdate`.
Read keys in `Update`, save the direction, then call `AddForce` in `FixedUpdate`.
Read keys in `Update`, then call `AddForce` in `Update`.

t_dc7fcd2a8e0a.explanation: `Update` runs every frame, so it reads and saves the current key direction. `FixedUpdate` runs at the physics step, where the script applies the push. The other choices apply force from a frame-based or camera-follow method, or read input only on the physics schedule. Review “Push the Ball with forces in FixedUpdate.”

t_a82450c2f443.prompt: A camera should stay 4 units above and 7 units behind a moving target. Which approach keeps that offset as the target moves?

choices.text: In `LateUpdate`, set camera position to target position plus `(0, 4, -7)`.
In `Start`, set camera position to target position plus `(0, 4, -7)`.
In `LateUpdate`, set camera position to target position minus `(0, 4, -7)`.
In `FixedUpdate`, set camera position to target position plus `(0, 4, -7)`.

t_a82450c2f443.explanation: Adding the offset places the camera at the target’s height plus 4 and 7 units back on the z axis. Repeating this in `LateUpdate` lets the camera catch up after the target’s frame updates. `Start` runs only once, subtraction reverses the offset, and `FixedUpdate` is the physics loop. Review “Make the camera follow the Ball.”

t_1af703b8efe4.prompt: A direction vector is `(3, 0, 4)`. What is the x component of its normalized vector? Give it to two decimal places.
t_1af703b8efe4.explanation: The vector’s length is 5, since √(3² + 4²) = 5. Divide each component by 5: x is 3 ÷ 5 = 0.60, y stays 0 and z is 4 ÷ 5 = 0.80. Normalizing makes the direction length 1. Review “Push the Ball with forces in FixedUpdate.”

t_14f08bd1cff9.prompt: In a few sentences, explain why the camera-follow script adds an offset to the target’s position in `LateUpdate`.
t_14f08bd1cff9.answer: The offset keeps the camera a fixed distance from the target, such as above and behind it. Adding the offset to the target’s current position updates the camera as the target moves. `LateUpdate` runs after `Update`, so the camera follows after the target has moved for that frame.
t_14f08bd1cff9.explanation: The offset describes the camera’s position relative to the target, and recalculating the position keeps that relationship as the target moves. `LateUpdate` runs after `Update`, so the camera catches up after the target’s frame updates. Review “Make the camera follow the Ball.”

t_d02f80124121.prompt: The Ball has a score of 4 and totalPickups is 6. One tagged pickup is collected, so the script adds 1 and then checks `if (score >= totalPickups)`. What happens?

t_ef1a43434ea1.prompt: Why does each hazard need a `Destroy` delay in Dodge, and how does an object pool handle finished objects differently?
t_ef1a43434ea1.answer: A delay removes each hazard after it is no longer needed, so hazards do not keep piling up. An object pool keeps objects for reuse: the game takes one when needed and returns it to the pool when finished.
t_ef1a43434ea1.explanation: `Destroy(gameObject, seconds)` removes a hazard after its delay, keeping old hazards from accumulating. An object pool reuses objects instead of repeatedly creating and destroying them. Review “Part 3: Learn the idea: read about reusing objects and watch how spawning works” and “Part 6: Destroy hazards you no longer need.”

t_1a22bcec213d.explanation: The hit sound changes the Player’s Audio Source pitch. Give the game-over tone its own Audio Source on GameManager so it stays at normal pitch. The other choices reuse the source whose pitch changes, assign a clip to the wrong kind of field, or change volume instead of pitch. See “Add a game over sound.”

t_d021762ddaf8.prompt: You want exactly 14 sparks when a hazard hits, with no sparks between hits. Which script action fits the particle setup?

choices.text: Call `sparks.Emit(14)` when the hit is handled.
Call `sparks.Play()` when the hit is handled.
Set Rate over Time to 14 and leave the system running.
Set Start Lifetime to 14 and restart the system.

t_d021762ddaf8.explanation: `Emit(14)` creates exactly 14 particles at that moment. `Play()` starts the system rather than specifying an exact burst count; Rate over Time makes particles appear over time; Start Lifetime controls how long particles last. See “Add a particle burst when you are hit.”

t_a5c8d37eba06.prompt: You want to know whether a lower hit volume improves Dodge. Which tuning approach gives you the clearest comparison?

choices.text: Change hit volume and spark speed, then play a run.
Change only hit volume, play a run, and judge it.
Change hit volume during Play and keep it when Play stops.
Change hit volume and pitch together, then judge both.

t_a5c8d37eba06.explanation: Changing one value per run lets you connect the difference you notice to that value. Changing volume with spark speed or pitch makes it unclear which change affected the feel. Changes to scene objects made during Play are undone when Play stops. See “Tune the feel one change at a time.”

t_5c73ed5a568e.prompt: With Play On Awake off and Rate over Time set to 0, `Emit(14)` cannot make a particle burst until Looping is turned on.

choices.text: True
False

t_5c73ed5a568e.explanation: `Emit(14)` makes a burst when the script calls it, even with Looping and Play On Awake off. Those settings keep the system quiet between hits. See “Add a particle burst when you are hit.”

t_6d82f2133099.prompt: You want to find out whether raising Sparks Start Speed improves a hit. Describe how to compare the old and new settings so you can tell what caused any difference.
t_6d82f2133099.answer: With Play off, record the current Start Speed, change only Start Speed, then play and judge a run. Stop Play before making another change. Keep the new value if it feels better; otherwise restore the old value.
t_6d82f2133099.explanation: A fair tuning comparison changes one value at a time, with Play off when editing, then uses a run to judge the result. See “Tune the feel one change at a time.”

t_e0f56e87ec66.title: Weekly builds: Dodge hit feedback and game feel
t_e0f56e87ec66.prompt:
This build contributes to Weekly builds, which counts for 40% of your course grade. You will make Dodge’s hits easier to hear and see, then tune one value and pick one spark color of your own.

In Dodge, tune one value on Hit Feedback or Sparks. Try a value different from the ones used in this week’s examples, changing only one value per run. Keep the setting you prefer. Choose a Start Color for Sparks that is different from orange. Record your final value and why you chose it, and name your color and why it suits your game in your LMS submission note. Record a fresh run that shows hazard hits with colored sparks and the game over panel, with sound if your recorder can capture it. On Windows the Game Bar records the game’s sound. The Mac’s built-in recorder does not: turn its microphone on and play through your speakers, or say in your note that the recording is silent. Your screenshots of the filled Hit Clip and Game Over Clip slots then count as the sound evidence. steps: With Play off, choose one value on Hit Feedback or Sparks to tune. Compare its current value with a different value, changing only that one value per run. Keep the value that gives you the feel you prefer and save the scene.

Change Sparks Start Color from orange to a color you choose. In your LMS submission note, name the color and explain why it suits your game. Also name the value you tuned, give its previous and final values, and explain your choice.

Upload the recording, both screenshots, and your note to the LMS by Sunday night this week. Note any help you used, including AI tools.

t_d4c1faaf50a9.prompt:

Your first post, due Thursday, shares one thing from your own week. Pick whichever fits you best:
- Something you saw in a playtest that surprised you, and what you did about it.
- The twist you chose (or are leaning toward), finishing this sentence: “My twist is ___ because I saw ___.” Say what you saw, not what you assumed.

Include the download link to your build and say whether it is for Windows or Mac. Add a screenshot or a short clip if you can, and say why you made the choice you did, not only what you made.

Your two replies, due Sunday night, each go to a different classmate. Download and run their build if you can, then tell them one thing that works and one thing you would change, and why. Base it on what you actually saw when you played, not on what you think of the idea. If you could not run their build, reply to what they described and say what you would test first.

How posts are graded, every week: full marks for a first post by Thursday that is about your own work and answers the prompt, and two replies by Sunday that each help a classmate go further (say what worked for you, suggest one change, or ask a real question). Late or one-line posts earn half.
followUps: You watched someone play without helping. What was the hardest moment to stay silent, and what did their hands do that their words never told you?

t_92d8c1f01b0e.prompt: Your Play button calls `SceneManager.LoadScene("Arena")`. What must be true for the call to load the game?

choices.text: Arena is open in the Scene view.
Arena is in the build’s scene list.
Arena has a MenuController component.
Arena is the first scene in the list.

t_92d8c1f01b0e.explanation: A scene can load by name only if it is included in the build’s scene list. Being open in the Editor or having a MenuController does not add it to the list. Arena does not need to be first; the menu should be first so the build opens there. Review “Add your scenes to the build and make it.”

t_aeb1f31591c0.prompt: You have a menu scene named StartScreen and a game scene named Arena. How should they appear in Build Profiles so the build opens at the menu and Play can load the game?

choices.text: StartScreen first, then Arena, with both scenes included.
Arena first, then StartScreen, with both scenes included.
StartScreen first, with Arena left out of the scene list.
Arena first, with StartScreen left out of the scene list.

t_aeb1f31591c0.explanation: The build opens the first scene in its list, so the menu belongs first. Both scenes must be included for the menu’s Play button to load the game. Review “Add your scenes to the build and make it.”

t_5c8fbf258f9f.prompt: You made a Windows build, but your classmate uses a Mac. What should you do so they can run your game?

choices.text: Share the Windows `.exe` and ask them to open it in Unity.
Share only the Windows `.exe` and rename it for macOS.
Find a playtester who uses Windows and share the complete build folder.
Build for Windows again and include both game scenes.

t_5c8fbf258f9f.explanation: A Windows build does not run on a Mac, so the page has you find a playtester on your own kind of computer and share the whole build folder. Opening the `.exe` in Unity, renaming it or adding scenes does not change the system the build was made for. Review “Share your build and playtest.”

t_ea15c3f15340.prompt: Which approach gives you useful evidence during a classmate’s playtest?

choices.text: Explain the controls as they play and note what they agree with.
Play their game yourself and guess where they may get stuck.
Ask what they thought before they try the game and record that.
Watch quietly and note pauses, movement, hits, and restarts.

t_ea15c3f15340.explanation: A playtest means watching someone else play without helping. Their actions can show where they pause, struggle, get hit, or restart. Explaining controls changes what you observe, and playing or asking beforehand does not show how they respond to the game on their own. Review “Share your build and playtest.”

t_b2a37de22f41.prompt: Suppose a playtester repeatedly overshoots safe gaps while dodging hazards. Write one sentence proposing a small change to how Dodge plays and linking it to what you observed.
t_b2a37de22f41.answer: I would reduce the Player’s movement speed slightly because the playtester repeatedly overshot safe gaps, then test whether that helps.
t_b2a37de22f41.explanation: A useful fix or twist makes one small gameplay change and has a reason grounded in something you saw during the playtest. The example answer links the observed overshooting to a single speed change that can be tested. Review “Share your build and playtest” and “Fix the problem, then add your twist.”

t_96683c57927e.prompt: A tile sprite is 24 pixels wide. You want it to occupy exactly one world unit. What Pixels Per Unit setting should you use?

choices.text: 24 pixels per unit
32 pixels per unit
48 pixels per unit
100 pixels per unit

t_96683c57927e.explanation: Pixels Per Unit tells Unity how many sprite pixels fit in one world unit, so 24 pixels at 24 Pixels Per Unit makes a one-unit tile. At 32, the tile would be 0.75 units wide; at 48, it would be 0.5 units wide; at 100, it would be 0.24 units wide. Review Part 1, “Start Hop and import your sprites.”

t_b2deb9e28211.prompt: You imported ground and platform sprites. Which setup lets you paint those pictures into a level on a grid?

choices.text: Create a Physics Material, add the sprites, then paint cells on a Rigidbody 2D
Create a Sprite Atlas, add the sprites, then paint cells on a Composite Collider 2D
Create a Tile Palette, add the sprites, then paint cells on a Canvas
Create a Tile Palette, add the sprites, then paint cells on a Tilemap

t_b2deb9e28211.explanation: A Tile Palette holds tiles made from sprites, and you paint those tiles onto a Tilemap in the grid. A Physics Material sets physics properties, a Sprite Atlas groups sprites, and a Canvas is used for UI. Review Part 2, “Make tiles and paint your level.” The 2D tilemap and Tile Palette tools are also listed in the instructor’s version notes, passage 9.

t_a9de14458135.prompt: Hero falls through the level. Which component pair belongs on Hero so physics can move it and it can touch the level’s 2D colliders?

choices.text: Rigidbody and Box Collider
Rigidbody 2D and Mesh Collider
Rigidbody 2D and Box Collider 2D
Sprite Renderer and Tilemap Collider 2D

t_a9de14458135.explanation: Rigidbody 2D lets physics move Hero, and Box Collider 2D gives Hero a shape that can touch the level. The unqualified Rigidbody and Box Collider are 3D components. Mesh Collider is also a 3D collider, and a Sprite Renderer only draws the sprite. Review Part 4, “Add Hero with a Rigidbody 2D and a collider.” The 2D physics component names are listed in the instructor’s version notes, passage 9.

t_a22e1cc2ee3f.prompt: In a new Universal 2D project, `Input.GetAxis` is the supported way to read movement keys.

choices.text: True
False

t_a22e1cc2ee3f.explanation: New projects use the Input System package only. The old `Input` class, including `Input.GetAxis`, throws an error when the game runs. The Move action can be read through the Input System. Review Part 5, “Make Hero run.” The version note about the old Input class is in passage 6; passage 9 confirms the project’s Move action works in 2D.

t_ab9ad391ac3c.prompt: In your own words, describe how Hero’s jump check should tell the difference between standing on a platform and touching its side. Include what the check looks for and where it is placed.
t_ab9ad391ac3c.answer: A thin box placed at Hero’s feet checks whether a collider on the Ground layer overlaps it. The box is narrower than Hero, so a platform’s side cannot reach it; Hero can jump only when ground is directly beneath the feet.
t_ab9ad391ac3c.explanation: The feet check looks only for Ground-layer colliders in a thin box below Hero. Keeping it narrower than Hero stops a wall at Hero’s side from counting as ground, so tapping jump against a wall does not allow wall climbing. Review Part 6, “Make Hero jump.”

t_e59f39b5fc8d.prompt: What is the difference between an Animation Clip and an Animator Controller?

choices.text: A clip chooses which state plays; a controller stores each sprite’s timing.
A clip detects ground contact; a controller moves Hero across the level.
A clip stores which sprite appears over time; a controller chooses which clip plays.
A clip stores keyboard input; a controller changes the camera position.

t_e59f39b5fc8d.explanation: An Animation Clip records changes over time, such as which sprite to show. The Animator Controller uses states, parameters, and transitions to choose a clip. The option about detecting ground contact confuses animation with a ground check. The option about keyboard input confuses animation with input handling. The option about moving the camera confuses animation with camera movement. Review “Make the Idle, Run and Jump clips” and “Connect the clips and make Hero play them.”

t_74332154a4fb.prompt: Hero is in the air, so isGrounded is false. Which Animator transition condition sends Hero to the jump state?

choices.text: Hero_Idle to Hero_Jump when isRunning is true.
Any State to Hero_Jump when isGrounded is false.
Hero_Run to Hero_Idle when isGrounded is false.
Hero_Jump to Hero_Run when isRunning is false.

t_74332154a4fb.explanation: The Any State transition to Hero_Jump uses isGrounded set to false, so Hero can enter the jump state from either idle or running. An isRunning condition describes sideways motion, not being airborne. A false ground check should not send Hero back to idle. The lesson’s controller has no Hero_Jump to Hero_Run transition. Review “Build the controller.”

t_525e98941303.prompt: When Hero touches a coin’s trigger, the coin can add one to the count and then remove itself from the scene.

choices.text: True
False

t_525e98941303.explanation: The coin’s trigger detects Hero, calls the counter to add one, and destroys the coin object. Review “Count coins with TextMeshPro.”

t_b4a759ac2701.prompt: Why does the camera follow script move the camera in LateUpdate?

choices.text: It follows after the player has moved for the frame.
It follows before the player reads any input.
It follows only when the player touches a trigger.
It follows at fixed intervals set by the physics engine.

t_b4a759ac2701.explanation: LateUpdate runs after the frame’s Update calls, so the camera can follow the player’s current position after movement. Following before input would not ensure the player has moved. Trigger contact is unrelated to camera timing. FixedUpdate is tied to physics steps; the camera script uses LateUpdate. Review “Make the camera follow Hero.”

t_8a62ac18de46.prompt: In one or two sentences, explain how you would decide whether a feature belongs in Must when scoping a game, and what to do with a feature that is not essential to the core loop.

t_8a62ac18de46.explanation: Must features support the game’s core loop and fit the available time. Features the game can work without can be moved to Should or Could. Review “Scope a game you can finish.”

f_b2f946aa0fb7.question: Unity Hub says there is no license, or a project refuses to open. What do I do?
f_b2f946aa0fb7.answer: The license is probably missing or tied to a different Unity ID. First, in Unity Hub click the gear at the top right, choose Licenses, and look for a Unity Personal license. Second, if the list is empty, click Add license, choose the free Unity Personal option and follow the prompts. Third, check that you are signed in with the same Unity ID you used before. Fourth, open the project again from Projects. If it still will not open, ask in the course Q&A forum and say which step you reached.

f_6f4964bdb59f.question: The download or install stops moving, or the Installs list shows it as failed. What do I do?
f_6f4964bdb59f.answer: Large downloads fail when the connection drops or the disk is nearly full. First, check that your internet is working and that you have about 20 GB of free disk space. Second, in Installs, use the retry option on the entry, or click Install Editor again and choose the same version. The install resumes where it stopped. Third, if 6.6 is not listed, use the download archive link on that screen, find 6000.6.4 and click its install button. Fourth, if your computer belongs to a school or employer and blocks the install, ask its IT help desk to install Unity Hub and Unity 6.6. If none of this works, ask in the course Q&A forum.

f_7d967ab62f1d.question: The Editor looks frozen after I click Create project, or my title bar shows another version. What do I do?
f_7d967ab62f1d.answer: If the Editor looks frozen, the first open compiles and imports files and can take five minutes or more. Wait until the progress bar at the bottom of the window is gone. If the title bar does not read like SampleScene - Courtyard - Windows, Mac, Linux - Unity 6.6 (6000.6.4f1), you made the project with the wrong version or template. First, close the Editor. Second, in Unity Hub click New project and check that the Editor version at the top reads 6000.6.4f1 or another 6000.6 version. Third, open the dropdown beside the search box, choose Core and click Universal 3D. Fourth, create the project again as a local project. If creating keeps failing, download the starter project from this page. Ask in the course Q&A forum if that fails too.

f_383feedef9f8.question: My Courtyard looks wrong: an object floats, sinks or lies flat, or the Game view is cropped or cut off. What do I do?
f_383feedef9f8.answer: The cause is almost always one number in the Transform or the camera. First, click the object in the Hierarchy and compare its Position, Rotation and Scale with the list on this page. A new object appears where the Scene view is looking, so every value must be typed. Second, check that Position Y is half the object’s height after scaling. Third, if you cannot see an object in the Scene view, click it in the Hierarchy, move the pointer over the Scene view and press F. Fourth, if the Game view is cut off, click the Game tab and choose 16:9 Aspect. Then select Main Camera and check that Position is 0, 16, -16, Rotation is 45, 0, 0 and Field of View is 60. If it still does not match, open the finished project from this page and compare. Ask in the course Q&A forum and attach a screenshot.

f_78d767e76c96.question: I cannot find Universal 3D in Unity Hub. What do I do?
f_78d767e76c96.answer: You see only the Learning templates. 1. In Unity Hub, click Projects, then New project. 2. Open the dropdown beside the search box. 3. Choose Core. 4. Click Universal 3D. Also check that the Editor version at the top reads 6000.6.4f1, or another 6000.6 version. If it does not, click Installs, then Install Editor, and add Unity 6.6. If the fix does not work, ask in the course Q&A forum.

f_27f5744c8bd3.question: The ball just hangs in the air when I press Play, or it falls straight through the ramp. Why?
f_27f5744c8bd3.answer: If the ball never moves, it has no Rigidbody. 1. Stop Play. 2. Click Ball in the Hierarchy. 3. Click Add Component, type Rigidbody and choose Rigidbody, not Rigidbody 2D. 4. Check that Use Gravity is ticked. If the ball falls through the ramp or floor, a collider is switched off. 1. Stop Play. 2. Tick the checkbox beside Sphere Collider on Ball. 3. Tick the checkbox beside Box Collider on Ramp and Floor. If the ball misses the ramp, check that Ball is at Position 0, 6, -7 and Ramp is at 0, 2, -4. If it still behaves wrongly, ask in the course Q&A forum.

f_8988c99fca08.question: I changed a value while the game was running, and it went back when I stopped. What happened?
f_8988c99fca08.answer: Changes made during Play are thrown away when you stop. This is how Unity works, so nothing is broken. 1. Click Play again to stop the game. The Play button is no longer lit. 2. Select the object in the Hierarchy. 3. Type the value again in the Inspector. 4. Choose File > Save. Make every fix while Play is off. If a value will not stay, ask in the course Q&A forum.

f_4c1722fdb1ad.question: My material color will not change, or the walls are still gray. How do I fix it?
f_4c1722fdb1ad.answer: If the color will not change, you probably clicked a different box. 1. Select the material in the Project window. 2. In the Inspector, find Surface Inputs. 3. Click the color box beside Base Map. 4. In the Color window, click the Hexadecimal box, type the code and press Enter. If the Hexadecimal box is missing, make the window taller and check that the mode dropdown reads RGB 0-255. If an object is still gray, the drag missed it. Drag the material from the Project window onto the object’s name in the Hierarchy, once for each wall. If the color still will not change, ask in the course Q&A forum.

f_904e5faf428b.question: Unity says “All compiler errors have to be fixed before you can enter playmode!” and Play will not start. What do I do?
f_904e5faf428b.answer: This means the Console holds at least one red error. Click the Console tab and find the first error in the list. Read its file, line and column, code and sentence, for example Assets/Scripts/Spinner.cs(17,45): error CS1002: ; expected. Double-click the message: Visual Studio Code opens with the cursor on that line. Fix it, and if the line looks fine, check the line above it. Save with Ctrl+S on Windows or Cmd+S on a Mac, click back into Unity and wait for the spinning compile icon to stop. If an old message stays, click Clear. Several errors at once are often one mistake, so fix the first one and look again. If it still fails, compare your file line by line with the code on the page, then ask in the course’s Q&A forum and paste the exact error text.

f_5ba3d23328d2.question: I cannot attach Spinner to the cube. Unity says “No MonoBehaviour scripts in the file, or their names do not match the file name.” What is wrong?
f_5ba3d23328d2.answer: The file name and the class name differ, often by one capital letter. The class inside the file takes the name you typed when you created the script, and Unity matches it to the file name. 1. In the Project window, check the script is called Spinner with a capital S. 2. If it is not, delete the script in the Project window. 3. Choose Assets > Create > MonoBehaviour Script, type Spinner and press Enter straight away. 4. Wait for Unity to finish compiling, then drag it onto Pickup_Test again, or use Add Component, type Spinner and press Enter. If the problem stays, check the Console for compiler errors, then ask in the course’s Q&A forum.

f_862b5ef3491d.question: I pressed Play and the cube does not move. There is no error. Why?
f_862b5ef3491d.answer: The script runs only when everything is in place. Check these in order. 1. Did you save Spinner.cs? Save with Ctrl+S on Windows or Cmd+S on a Mac, click back into Unity and wait for compiling to finish. 2. Click Pickup_Test and scroll to the bottom of the Inspector. Is there a Spinner (Script) section? If not, attach the script again. 3. Is Is Spinning ticked? 4. Is Speed more than 0? Remember that the Inspector value wins over the number in the code, so a Speed of 0 there will keep the cube still. If you changed a value during Play, it is thrown away when you stop, so change it with Play off. 5. Look in the Scene tab: the Game view may not show the cube. If it still does not move, ask in the course’s Q&A forum and attach a screenshot of the Inspector.

f_3295641a6b79.question: I changed the number in my code, but the cube still turns at the old speed. Which value is used?
f_3295641a6b79.answer: The Inspector value wins. The number in the code is only the starting value, used when the script is first attached. After that the component keeps its own copy. To use the new number from the code, click Pickup_Test, click the three-dot menu in the Spinner (Script) heading and choose Reset. Or type the value you want into Speed in the Inspector. Each cube keeps its own Speed, so check both Pickup_Test and Pickup_Test_B. If the value still looks wrong, ask in the course’s Q&A forum.

f_421d2c156552.question: I press W and nothing happens, or the Ball does not move. What do I do?
f_421d2c156552.answer:
1. Click once inside the Game view. Keys go to the window you clicked last, and after you type in the Inspector, the Inspector has your keys.
2. Select Ball and check that the Inspector shows a Ball Controller (Script) section. If it is missing, click Add Component, type BallController and press Enter.
3. Check that Force reads 20 and that you edited it with Play off. Changes made during Play are thrown away when Play stops.
4. Look at the Console for a red line and fix the first error in the list.
If it still does not work, post in the course’s Q&A forum with a screenshot of the Ball’s Inspector and the Console.

f_45bf86a4991e.question: The Console says: error CS0103: The name ‘Keyboard’ does not exist in the current context. Or it shows CS0246 or CS0103 on another line. How do I fix it?
f_45bf86a4991e.answer:
1. Double-click the error in the Console. Visual Studio Code opens at the line.
2. Check that the top of BallController has the line `using UnityEngine.InputSystem;`. Without it, Keyboard is an unknown name.
3. Compare the line letter by letter with the code on the page. Capital letters, brackets and semicolons all matter. For example, `Keyboard.current.wKey` needs a capital K and a lowercase w.
4. If several errors are listed, fix the first one only, save with Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac), and look again. Later errors are often caused by the first.
If the first error will not go away, ask in the course’s Q&A forum and paste the exact error text.

f_fd2eefa0a080.question: The Console says: InvalidOperationException: You are trying to read Input using the UnityEngine.Input class. What went wrong?
f_fd2eefa0a080.answer:
1. This project uses the new Input System package only. Code that uses `Input.GetKey` or `Input.GetAxis` compiles but throws this error when the game runs.
2. Double-click the error in the Console to find the line that uses `Input.`
3. Replace it with the new way: `Keyboard.current.wKey.isPressed` while a key is held, or `Keyboard.current.wKey.wasPressedThisFrame` for the frame the key goes down.
4. Check that the file has `using UnityEngine.InputSystem;` at the top, then save and press Play again.
If the error stays, post in the course’s Q&A forum with the line of code that the Console points to.

f_1ca500e23d11.question: The Console says NullReferenceException in FixedUpdate, and the Ball does not move. What do I do?
f_1ca500e23d11.answer:
1. The script cannot find a Rigidbody. Select Ball in the Hierarchy and check that BallController is on the Ball, not on another object.
2. Check that the Ball has a Rigidbody section in the Inspector. If it does not, click Add Component, type Rigidbody and choose Rigidbody, not Rigidbody 2D.
3. Open BallController and check that Start contains `rb = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();`.
4. Save, wait for the spinner at the bottom right of the Editor to stop, and press Play again.
If it still fails, ask in the course’s Q&A forum and paste the full error line.

f_5b0d67455357.question: Why does the Ball bump off my Pickup instead of passing through it? Or why is the Console empty when I touch it?
f_5b0d67455357.answer: Two things cause this, so check both in order. 1. Click Pickup in the Hierarchy. In the Inspector, find Box Collider and tick Is Trigger. If it is not ticked, the cube blocks the Ball like a wall and the touch never reaches your script. 2. Check the spelling. The tag on the Pickup must be Pickup with a capital P, and the script must say `other.CompareTag("Pickup")` with the same spelling. Also check the method is named exactly `OnTriggerEnter`, with those capitals, or Unity never calls it. Click Ball and make sure it still has its Rigidbody. Save, wait for the spinning icon to stop, and press Play again. If the Ball still bumps the cube or the Console stays empty, post in the course Q&A forum with a screenshot of the Pickup’s Inspector.

f_b0f6cb1e28ad.question: The Console shows a red line: error CS1022: Type or namespace definition, or end-of-file expected. What did I do wrong?
f_b0f6cb1e28ad.answer: This error means a curly brace is in the wrong place, usually in BallController. 1. Double-click the red line in the Console. Visual Studio Code opens the file near the problem. 2. Look at the end of the file. The new method `OnTriggerEnter` must sit above the final }, which closes the class. If it sits below it, move it up inside. 3. Count the braces. Every { needs a matching }. Look for one that is missing or doubled after you pasted. 4. Save the file with Ctrl+S (Command+S on a Mac), click back into Unity, and wait for the spinning icon at the bottom right to stop. If the red line stays, ask in the course Q&A forum and paste the exact error text and the last 15 lines of your file.

f_919a3a4e7a5e.question: As soon as I press Play, a red NullReferenceException says Object reference not set to an instance of an object. Why?
f_919a3a4e7a5e.answer: The script is trying to change a text object it cannot find. 1. Stop Play. Click Ball in the Hierarchy. 2. In the Inspector, find Ball Controller (Script). Look at Score Text and Win Text. If either reads None, that is the cause. 3. Drag ScoreText from the Hierarchy onto Score Text. Drag WinText onto Win Text. 4. Click Play again. If both boxes were already filled, check that you did not delete or rename the text objects, and that Ball Controller is on the Ball. If the error stays, ask in the course Q&A forum and include the full red line from the Console.

f_14f066445e03.question: The error CS0246 says the type or namespace name ‘TMP_Text’ could not be found. How do I fix it?
f_14f066445e03.answer: Unity does not know what TMP_Text is, because the script is missing its using line. 1. Open BallController in Visual Studio Code. 2. At the very top, under the other using lines, check for `using TMPro;`. Add it if it is missing. 3. Check the spelling and capitals: T, M, P and O are capitals, and the line ends with a semicolon. 4. Save, click back into Unity, and wait for the spinning icon to stop. If a TMP Importer window ever opens, click Import TMP Essentials first. If the error remains, ask in the course Q&A forum.

f_cb8cfb330332.question: Unity says “UnassignedReferenceException: The variable hazardPrefab of HazardSpawner has not been assigned”, or “ArgumentException: The Object you want to instantiate is null”. Nothing falls. What do I do?
f_cb8cfb330332.answer:
What you see: red lines in the Console as soon as the spawner tries to make its first hazard. Both messages have one cause: the Hazard Prefab slot is empty.
1. Click Play to stop.
2. In the Hierarchy, click Spawner.
3. In the Inspector, find Hazard Spawner (Script). Its Hazard Prefab field reads None (Game Object).
4. In the Project window, click the Prefabs folder and drag the Hazard prefab onto that field.
5. Choose File > Save, then click Play again.
If the field is full and the error stays, ask in the course’s Q&A forum. Paste the full red line from the Console and say which part you are on.
Note: drag the prefab from the Prefabs folder, not a Hazard from the Hierarchy. The Hierarchy should hold no Hazard of its own.

f_5129bafe79c6.question: I press Play and no hazards appear, and the Console shows no error. Why?
f_5129bafe79c6.answer:
What you see: the Player moves, the Floor is there, and the Hierarchy never shows a Hazard(Clone).
1. Click Play to stop.
2. In the Hierarchy, click Spawner. Check that Hazard Spawner (Script) is listed in the Inspector. If it is not, drag HazardSpawner from the Scripts folder onto Spawner.
3. Check that the Hazard Prefab field holds Hazard.
4. Check that the script file is saved. Click back into Unity and wait for the spinning icon at the bottom right to stop.
5. Click Play again, then click once inside the Game view.
If nothing appears, ask in the course’s Q&A forum and say which of these checks you did.

f_c67045f011c4.question: The hazards fall straight through the Floor, or hang in the air and never fall. What is wrong?
f_c67045f011c4.answer:
What you see: in Play, a hazard drops through the Floor and out of sight, or it stays where it appears.
If it falls through:
1. Click Play to stop.
2. Click Floor in the Hierarchy.
3. In the Inspector, check that Box Collider is listed. If it is missing, choose Component > Physics > Box Collider.
If it hangs in the air:
1. In the Project window, open the Prefabs folder and click the Hazard prefab.
2. Check that Rigidbody is listed. If not, click Add Component, type Rigidbody and press Enter. Choose Rigidbody, not Rigidbody 2D.
3. Check that Use Gravity is ticked.
4. Choose File > Save and try Play again.
If it still fails, ask in the course’s Q&A forum.

f_11d13b667f63.question: Hazards never vanish and the Hierarchy list keeps growing, or hazards vanish the moment they appear. How do I fix it?
f_11d13b667f63.answer:
What you see: either more and more Hazard(Clone) entries pile up, or each one disappears at once.
If they never vanish:
1. In the Project window, open the Prefabs folder and click the Hazard prefab.
2. In the Inspector, look for Hazard Lifetime (Script). If it is missing, click Add Component, type HazardLifetime and press Enter.
3. Choose File > Save.
If they vanish at once:
1. Click the Hazard prefab in the Prefabs folder.
2. In Hazard Lifetime (Script), type 6 into Lifetime.
3. Click Play to test.
If you see “Can’t add script component ‘HazardLifetime’ because the script class cannot be found”, check that the file is named HazardLifetime, save it, and read the Console for a red line that names a file and line number.
If none of this works, ask in the course’s Q&A forum.

f_56a341c14f95.question: The Console shows `NullReferenceException` pointing at `GameManager.UpdateLivesText`, or `UnassignedReferenceException: The variable gameOverPanel of GameManager has not been assigned`. What do I do?
f_56a341c14f95.answer:
This means a box on the Game Manager (Script) is empty.
1. Click Play to stop the game.
2. In the Hierarchy, click GameManager.
3. In the Inspector, find the box named in the message: Lives Text or Game Over Panel.
4. Drag LivesText (or GameOverPanel) from the Hierarchy into that box.
5. Choose File > Save, then press Play again.
If the fix does not work, ask in this course’s Q&A forum and include a screenshot of the Inspector and the Console.

f_6419de999796.question: I hit a hazard and Lives never drops, or the Console shows `NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object` pointing at PlayerHit. What is wrong?
f_6419de999796.answer:
Work through these checks in order.
1. Click Player in the Hierarchy and check that Player Hit (Script) is in the Inspector. If it is not, use Add Component and add PlayerHit.
2. In the Project window, click the Hazard prefab, not a copy in the scene. Check that its Tag reads Hazard. If it does not, open the Tag dropdown and choose Hazard.
3. In the Hierarchy, check that a GameManager object exists and that it shows Game Manager (Script). The NullReferenceException appears when it is missing.
4. Save, press Play and click once inside the Game view before you steer.
If the fix does not work, ask in this course’s Q&A forum and paste the full Console message.

f_497d3a16c173.question: Restart does nothing when I click it, or the game is frozen after I restart. How do I fix it?
f_497d3a16c173.answer:
Take the two cases one at a time.
Restart does nothing:
1. Click RestartButton in the Hierarchy and find On Click () in the Button component.
2. Check that the box holds GameManager from the Hierarchy, not the script file from the Project window.
3. Check that the dropdown reads GameManager > Restart ().
4. Check that EventSystem is still in the Hierarchy. If it is missing, choose GameObject > UI (Canvas) > Event System.
The game is frozen after restarting:
1. Open GameManager in Visual Studio Code.
2. Check that `Time.timeScale = 1f;` is the first line in `Start`. Time stays at 0 until you set it back.
3. Save the file and test again.
If the fix does not work, ask in this course’s Q&A forum.

f_4920f8fe81b3.question: The Console shows `error CS0103: The name 'SceneManager' does not exist in the current context`, or `error CS0246: The type or namespace name 'TMP_Text' could not be found`. What do I change?
f_4920f8fe81b3.answer:
Both errors mean a `using` line is missing at the top of GameManager.
1. Open GameManager in Visual Studio Code.
2. For the SceneManager error, add `using UnityEngine.SceneManagement;`.
3. For the TMP_Text error, add `using TMPro;`. Check the spelling and capital letters.
4. Save the file (Ctrl+S on Windows, Command+S on a Mac), return to Unity and wait for the red lines to disappear.
If you see `error CS1002: ; expected`, read the line number in the message and add the missing semicolon at the end of that line.
If the fix does not work, ask in this course’s Q&A forum and paste the whole error line.

f_181e8952c11d.question: I click Play and get hit, but I hear nothing and there is no red error. What do I check?
f_181e8952c11d.answer:
1. In the Game view toolbar, check that Mute Audio is not switched on, and turn up your computer volume.
2. Click hit in the Audio folder and press the preview play button in the Inspector. If the preview is silent too, the problem is your volume or the file, not your script.
3. Click Player and find the Audio Source. Check that Hit Clip on Hit Feedback (Script) is filled with hit.
4. Click inside the Game view once after pressing Play, so the game has focus, then move into a hazard with W, A, S and D.
Still silent? Post in the course’s Q&A forum with a screenshot of the Player’s Inspector.

f_29aa017cf258.question: The Console says NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object, and the message mentions HitFeedback.Play or GameManager.GameOver. What is wrong?
f_29aa017cf258.answer:
A slot in the Inspector is empty, so the script has nothing to use.
1. Stop Play. Changes made during Play are undone anyway.
2. If the message names HitFeedback.Play, click Player. In Hit Feedback (Script), check that Hit Source, Hit Clip and Sparks are all filled, not None. Drag Player onto Hit Source, hit onto Hit Clip, and Sparks from the Hierarchy onto Sparks.
3. If the message names GameManager.GameOver, click GameManager. Drag GameManager onto Game Over Source and gameover onto Game Over Clip.
4. Choose File > Save and press Play again.
Still red? Ask in the course’s Q&A forum and paste the full error line.

f_b8e3070d7509.question: Unity shows error CS0122: ‘HitFeedback.Play()’ is inaccessible due to its protection level, or error CS1061: ‘HitFeedback’ does not contain a definition for ‘Play’. How do I fix it?
f_b8e3070d7509.answer:
Both errors mean PlayerHit cannot find the method it wants to call.
1. For CS0122, open HitFeedback and make sure the line reads `public void Play()`. The word public must be there. If the same error names ‘GameManager.LoseLife()’, add public to LoseLife in GameManager.
2. For CS1061, check the spelling. The method must be `Play` with a capital P in both HitFeedback and PlayerHit.
3. Save each file with Ctrl+S on Windows or Command+S on a Mac, return to Unity, and wait until the Console shows no red lines.
Still stuck? Post both files in the course’s Q&A forum.

f_c7425dcab3ef.question: I typed a new Pitch or Spark Count value, pressed Play, and after stopping it went back to the old number. Or every hit still sounds the same. What happened?
f_c7425dcab3ef.answer:
1. You most likely edited the value while Play was on. Changes to scene objects are undone when Play stops. Stop Play, type the value again, then press Play.
2. Pitch Min, Pitch Max, Hit Volume and Spark Count belong to Hit Feedback (Script) on Player. Click Player, not another object.
3. If every hit sounds the same, check that Pitch Min is 0.9 and Pitch Max is 1.1, so they are not equal, and that you saved the script.
4. Two hits can sound alike by chance. Play several runs before you decide pitch is not varying.
Still the same? Ask in the course’s Q&A forum and say which value you changed.

f_16392c2ee4e5.question: Why does the Console say Scene ‘SampleScene’ couldn’t be loaded because it has not been added to the build settings, and Play does nothing?
f_16392c2ee4e5.answer: The scene is not in the build’s scene list, and a scene can only be loaded if it is in that list. Fix it in order: 1. Open SampleScene from the Scenes folder in the Project window. 2. Choose File > Build Profiles. 3. Click Add Open Scenes, so SampleScene joins the list. 4. Check that MainMenu is first, numbered 0, SampleScene is second, numbered 1, and both boxes are ticked. 5. Close the window, then build again, because an old build does not pick up the change. Also check that the Game Scene Name field on the MenuController object reads SampleScene. If it still fails, ask in the Q&A forum and paste the exact Console line.

f_ce8018d914a4.question: I clicked a button and nothing happened. Why is PlayGame() or QuitGame() missing from the On Click dropdown, or why does it say No Function?
f_ce8018d914a4.answer: Fix it in order: 1. Open the MenuController script in Visual Studio Code. Check that both methods say `public void`, because only public methods appear in the dropdown. 2. Save the file, return to Unity and wait until the Console shows no red lines. 3. Click the button in the Hierarchy and look at its On Click () list. 4. Drag the MenuController object from the Hierarchy into the field that reads None (Object). Do not drag the script file from the Project window: then the dropdown offers only items such as GameObject. 5. Open the dropdown that reads No Function and choose MenuController > PlayGame() or MenuController > QuitGame(). 6. Save the scene. Remember that Quit does nothing visible in the Editor: look for Quit pressed in the Console. If it still fails, ask in the Q&A forum.

f_5e0223644005.question: Why is my menu panel pale or see-through, or why are my title and buttons missing?
f_5e0223644005.answer: There are two usual causes. For a pale or see-through panel: 1. Click Panel in the Hierarchy. 2. In the Inspector, click the color box beside Color on the Image component. 3. In the window titled Color, set A to 255. 4. Check that the Hexadecimal box reads 1B1F3B. For a title or buttons that are hidden, the Panel is drawn on top of them. In the Hierarchy, drag Panel to the top of the list inside Canvas, above TitleText, so it is drawn first. Then save with File > Save. If the Game view still looks wrong, ask in the Q&A forum and add a screenshot.

f_5210866fd023.question: Why does the Console show a red error when I press Left Shift, or why does Visual Studio Code or Unity say The type or namespace name ‘Keyboard’ could not be found?
f_5210866fd023.answer: The error text tells you which cause it is. If you see The type or namespace name ‘Keyboard’ could not be found: 1. Open SlowFocus in Visual Studio Code. 2. Check that the first lines include `using UnityEngine.InputSystem;`, spelled exactly like that. 3. Save, return to Unity and wait for the Console to settle. If Left Shift does nothing and nothing is red: click inside the Game view first, so it has focus, and hold the key again. Do not use `Input.GetKey`: this version of Unity throws an error for the old Input class. If it still fails, ask in the Q&A forum and paste the whole red line.

f_414115178d5d.question: Why can’t I find Tilemap in the GameObject menu, or why does the Hierarchy show a Directional Light and no Global Light 2D?
f_414115178d5d.answer: What you see: GameObject > 2D Object has no Tilemap entry, and the Hierarchy holds Main Camera, Directional Light and Global Volume. Fix, in order: 1. Look at the Editor window title and the Hierarchy. A Directional Light means Hop was made from Universal 3D, and the 3D project has no Sprites or Tilemap entries. 2. Open Unity Hub, click Projects, then New project. 3. Open the dropdown beside the search box and choose Core. 4. Click Universal 2D, check the Editor version reads 6000.6.4f1, open the Project name dropdown, choose Create new local project and type Hop. 5. Redo the sprite import and the tiles in the new project. Nothing in your Dodge project is affected.

f_1a15325bd9ea.question: Why is nothing painting, and why does the Tile Palette window show no tiles?
f_1a15325bd9ea.answer: What you see: you click in the Scene view and no tile appears, or the Tile Palette window is empty. Fix, in order: 1. In the Tile Palette window, open the palette dropdown at the top and choose HopPalette. If it is empty, select Grass and Dirt in Assets > Sprites and drag them into the palette’s grid area, saving the tiles in the Tiles folder. 2. Set Active Tilemap to Level. 3. Click a tile in the palette so it is selected. 4. Choose the Paint tool (B) or Box Fill (U). 5. If the Scene view looks tilted, click the 2D button in the Scene view toolbar. 6. To undo a misplaced tile, press Ctrl+Z (Command+Z on a Mac), or use the Erase tool (D).

f_c6131683841d.question: Why does Hero fall through the floor, or why does the whole level fall away when I press Play?
f_c6131683841d.answer: What you see: in Play, Hero drops out of the bottom of the Game view, or the floor and platforms drop with it. Fix, in order: 1. Click Hero and check it has both a Rigidbody 2D and a Box Collider 2D. Add what is missing with Add Component, and pick Rigidbody 2D, not Rigidbody. 2. Click Level and check it has a Tilemap Collider 2D and a Composite Collider 2D. If Composite Operation is missing, add the Tilemap Collider 2D first, then the Composite Collider 2D again. 3. On Level’s Rigidbody 2D, set Body Type to Static. A Dynamic body falls under gravity, and the level falls with it. 4. On the Tilemap Collider 2D, set Composite Operation to Merge. You should then see one outline round the floor and one round each platform. 5. Save with File > Save and press Play again.

f_a83a4cf57f47.question: Why does the Console show red errors when I press Play, such as InvalidOperationException or NullReferenceException?
f_a83a4cf57f47.answer: What you see: red lines in the Console, and Hero does not run. Fix, in order: 1. If the error is InvalidOperationException about the Input class, your script uses the old input, such as Input.GetAxis or Input.GetKey. This project reads input with the Input System only. Replace the whole file with the code on this week’s page. If a box titled Script Updating Consent opens, click No and fix the line by hand. 2. If the error is NullReferenceException at HeroController, click Hero and check it has a Rigidbody 2D. Then check that the text in FindAction(“Move”) matches exactly, capital M included. 3. If the error is UnassignedReferenceException saying feetCheck has not been assigned, drag FeetCheck from the Hierarchy onto the Feet Check field in the Hero Controller component. 4. Click the first red line to see which file and line it points to. Fix it, save, and wait for the Console to clear before pressing Play.

f_7331f99aa71f.question: My Hero stays in the jump pose on the ground, and the Console may show a red NullReferenceException on the line with feetCheck.position. What do I check?
f_7331f99aa71f.answer:
1. Click Hero in the Hierarchy and open its children. Check there is a child named exactly FeetCheck, with the same capital letters, and that it sits at Hero’s feet.
2. Click your Level object and check its Layer is set to Ground. HeroAnimation only counts Hero as grounded when the box at FeetCheck touches the Ground layer.
3. Open HeroController and HeroAnimation and check the OverlapBox size is the same in both: new Vector2(0.7f, 0.1f).
4. Press Play again. If the error is still there, the child name is the most likely cause: rename it to FeetCheck.

f_7a924630ddfa.question: The Console shows a yellow warning: Parameter ‘isRunning’ does not exist. Hero never switches clips. What do I do?
f_7a924630ddfa.answer:
1. Choose Window > Animation > Animator and click the Parameters tab.
2. Compare the two names, letter by letter, with the quoted names in HeroAnimation: “isRunning” and “isGrounded”. A capital I or a space makes them different.
3. Fix whichever side is wrong. Renaming the parameter in the Animator is usually quicker than editing the script.
4. Click Hero and check the Animator component has Controller set to Hero. Press Play and test again.

f_ff12b5b383f0.question: I touch a coin and nothing happens, or the Console shows a red UnassignedReferenceException or NullReferenceException. How do I fix it?
f_ff12b5b383f0.answer:
1. If the error says UnassignedReferenceException, click GameManager and look at Coin Counter in the Inspector. Drag CoinsText from the Hierarchy into the empty Coins Text slot.
2. If the error says NullReferenceException in CoinPickup, there is no CoinCounter in the scene. Check that GameManager exists and has the Coin Counter component.
3. If there is no error but the coin stays, click the Coin prefab in the Prefabs folder. Check Circle Collider 2D has Is Trigger ticked and that Coin Pickup is attached.
4. Click Hero and check its Tag is Player. CoinPickup ignores anything else.
5. Save with File > Save and press Play again.

f_2c406501fd23.question: The Game view shows the camera not moving, everything has disappeared, or the screen shakes when Hero runs. What is wrong?
f_2c406501fd23.answer:
1. If the camera does not move, click Main Camera. In Camera Follow, drag Hero from the Hierarchy into the empty Target slot. An empty Target also causes a red UnassignedReferenceException.
2. If everything disappeared, the camera’s Z position was changed. Set Transform > Position Z on Main Camera back to -10.
3. If the screen shakes, check the script uses LateUpdate and not Update.
4. If it still shakes, stop Play. In HeroAnimation, add this line right after rb = GetComponent<Rigidbody2D>(); in Start: `rb.interpolation = RigidbodyInterpolation2D.Interpolate;`. Save, return to Unity and test again.

s_8030c87393a2.title: Instructor's version notes: Unity 6.6 (editor 6000.6.4), checked in the editor
s_8030c87393a2.text:
# Instructor's version notes: Unity 6.6 (editor 6000.6.4), checked in the editor

Use these names exactly: students see them on screen.

## Unity Hub
- Sidebar: Projects, Installs. Licenses are under Settings (the gear) > Licenses > Add license.
- Projects > New project. The screen opens on the "Learning" templates. Open the dropdown beside the search box and choose "Core" to see Universal 2D, Universal 3D, High Definition 3D and others. The Editor version is chosen at the top of this screen.
- With a template selected, the panel on the right shows Project name, Location and the Create project button. The Project name box is also a dropdown: students choose "Create new local project" (not the default, which connects to Unity Cloud), then type the name.

## A new Universal 3D project
- The window title reads: SampleScene - <project name> - Windows, Mac, Linux - Unity 6.6 (6000.6.4f1).
- Hierarchy: SampleScene with Main Camera, Directional Light and Global Volume.
- Project window, Assets folder: InputSystem_Actions, Readme, Scenes, Settings, TutorialInfo. The scene file is Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.
- On first open the Inspector shows a "URP Empty Template" readme with a "Remove Readme Assets" button.
- Windows in the Default layout: Hierarchy (left), Scene and Game tabs (center), Inspector (right), Project and Console tabs (bottom). Reset with Window > Layouts > Default.

## Menus (top menu bar)
- File: New Scene, Open Scene, Save, Save As..., Build Profiles, Build And Run. There is no "Build Settings". The Build Profiles window has "Scene List" at its top left (a new project already lists SampleScene; "Add Open Scenes" adds the open one) and no platform list until you click "Add Build Profile": the "Platform Browser" opens, with Windows, macOS and Linux under Desktop and an "Add Build Profile" button at the bottom right; the new profile is marked Active and "Build" is at the bottom. A Mac build also leaves a folder ending in "BackUpThisFolder_ButDontShipItWithYourGame".
- Edit: Undo, Redo, Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Play Mode, Project Settings... On a Mac, preferences are Unity > Settings...; on Windows, Edit > Preferences...
- GameObject > 3D Object: Cube, Sphere, Capsule, Cylinder, Plane, Quad, Text - TextMeshPro.
- GameObject > UI (Canvas): Image, Text - TextMeshPro, Panel, Button - TextMeshPro, Toggle, Slider, Canvas, Event System. The menu is named "UI (Canvas)", not "UI".
- GameObject > Visual Effects: Particle System, Trail, Line. GameObject > Audio: Audio Source. GameObject > Light: Directional Light, Point Light, Spot Light.
- Assets > Create: Folder, Material, MonoBehaviour Script, Scene, Scripting, Physics Material, Input Actions, Animation, 2D, TextMeshPro. A new script is Assets > Create > MonoBehaviour Script (also under Scripting > MonoBehaviour Script). A scene is Assets > Create > Scene > Scene; a prefab is made by dragging an object from the Hierarchy into the Project window.
- Component > Physics 2D: Rigidbody 2D, Box Collider 2D, Circle Collider 2D, Capsule Collider 2D, Composite Collider 2D.

## Code (C#), compiled in this version
- Input: new projects use the Input System package only. `Input.GetAxis`, `Input.GetKey` and the rest of the old Input class compile but throw InvalidOperationException when the game runs. Read keys with `Keyboard.current.aKey.isPressed`, `Keyboard.current.spaceKey.wasPressedThisFrame` (with `using UnityEngine.InputSystem;`), or use the project's own actions: `InputSystem.actions.FindAction("Move")` then `ReadValue<Vector2>()`. The template's InputSystem_Actions asset has a Player map with Move, Look, Attack, Interact, Crouch, Jump, Previous, Next, Sprint.
- Rigidbody: `rb.linearVelocity` and `rb.linearDamping`. `rb.velocity` is marked obsolete.
- Finding objects: `FindAnyObjectByType<T>()`. `FindFirstObjectByType<T>()` and `FindObjectOfType<T>()` are both marked obsolete in 6000.6 and give a yellow warning.
- Text: `using TMPro;` and `TMP_Text`. Scenes: `using UnityEngine.SceneManagement;` and `SceneManager.LoadScene(...)`.
- `AddForce`, `ForceMode.Impulse`, `OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)`, `CompareTag`, `Destroy`, `Instantiate`, `Time.deltaTime`, `[SerializeField]` are unchanged.

## The Inspector, as it reads in this version
- A new object made from the GameObject menu appears where the Scene view is looking, not at the origin: its Position is some uneven number. Students type 0, 0, 0 into Position (or use the three-dot menu on Transform > Reset) before the page gives positions.
- After creating an object or asset its name is in edit mode: type the name and press Enter.
- A primitive's Inspector reads, in order: Transform, "Cube (Mesh Filter)" (or "Sphere (Mesh Filter)"), its collider (Box Collider, Sphere Collider), Mesh Renderer, then the material, "Lit (Material)", grayed out because the default material cannot be edited, and the Add Component button.
- Sphere Collider: Edit Collider, Is Trigger, Provides Contacts, Material (shows "None (Physics Material)"), Center, Radius, Layer Overrides.
- Add Component opens a small search box: type the name and press Enter. Typing "Rigidbody" lists Rigidbody and Rigidbody 2D.
- Rigidbody: Mass (1), Linear Damping (0), Angular Damping (0.05), Automatic Center Of Mass, Automatic Tensor, Use Gravity (ticked), Is Kinematic, Interpolate (None), Collision Detection (Discrete), Constraints (Freeze Position X Y Z, Freeze Rotation X Y Z), Layer Overrides. There are no fields named "Drag" or "Angular Drag".
- A new material (Assets > Create > Material) uses the shader Universal Render Pipeline/Lit. Under Surface Inputs: Base Map with a color box beside it, Metallic Map with a slider, Smoothness with a slider at 0.5. The color of a material is the color box beside Base Map; there is no field called "Albedo" or "Color".
- Clicking a color box opens a window titled "Color": a color wheel, a mode dropdown showing "RGB 0-255", sliders R, G, B, A, a box labeled "Hexadecimal", and "Defaults" swatches. The box is "Hexadecimal", not "Hex Color".
- A material is put on an object by dragging it from the Project window onto the object in the Scene view or the Hierarchy.
- Directional Light: Light has four sections that open with a triangle: General, Emission, Rendering, Shadows. Under Emission: Light Appearance (set to "Filter and Temperature"), Filter, Temperature (5000), Intensity (2). To give the light a plain color, set Light Appearance to "Color".
- The Scene view has a column of tools at its top left (View, Move, Rotate, Scale, Rect, Transform; keys Q, W, E, R, T, Y) and the scene gizmo at its top right with "Persp" under it. Play, Pause and Step are at the top center of the Editor.
- Edit > Duplicate (Ctrl+D, Command+D on a Mac) names the copy "Ball (1)", selects it and does NOT start a rename. To rename a selected object: Edit > Rename (F2 on Windows, Enter on a Mac), type the name, press Enter.
- The Game view's aspect dropdown is the third control in its toolbar and reads "Free Aspect" in a new project. The choice is kept per project: each new project needs "16:9 Aspect" chosen again.
- Changes made during Play to objects in the scene (a Transform, a Rigidbody's Mass) are undone when Play stops. Changes to assets (a material's color or Smoothness, a physics material) are kept.
- An unsaved scene shows an asterisk after its name in the Hierarchy; do not rely on the title bar.
- A new Physics Material (Assets > Create > Physics Material): Bounciness 0, Bounce Combine Average. A ball with Bounciness 0.8 on a floor with no material bounces once; with Bounce Combine set to Maximum it bounces eight times or more.
- A new Point Light: Range 10, Intensity 1, no shadows: invisible on a floor 4 units below. Range does not make it brighter; Intensity 30 gives a clear pool of light. Lowering the Directional Light does not make the scene dark, because the sky still lights it.

## UI, text and effects, checked in this version
- The first time a TextMeshPro object is added (GameObject > UI (Canvas) > Text - TextMeshPro), a window titled "TMP Importer" opens: click "Import TMP Essentials", then "Import Anyway" in the box titled "Unofficial Unity source" that follows, wait, and close the window. Once per project; it can leave two red layout lines in the Console (Clear removes them).
- Adding the first UI object also adds a Canvas (components: Canvas, Canvas Scaler, Graphic Raycaster) and an EventSystem (components: Event System, Input System UI Input Module). The text object is named "Text (TMP)" and sits under Canvas; its component is "TextMeshPro - Text (UI)", and in code its type is TMP_Text (using TMPro;).
- A particle system is GameObject > Visual Effects > Particle System (there is no "Effects" menu). An audio source is GameObject > Audio > Audio Source, or Add Component > Audio Source.
- A prefab is made by dragging an object from the Hierarchy into a folder in the Project window.
- A UI object made from the menu bar lands directly under the Canvas, whatever is selected: to put it inside a panel, drag it onto the panel in the Hierarchy.
- Tags other than the built-in ones (Player, MainCamera, Finish...) are added with the Tag dropdown > Add Tag...
- If a script uses an API marked for automatic update (rb.velocity, rb.drag), a box titled "Script Updating Consent" asks whether to update the files: with the code on these pages it does not appear; a student who pasted old code should choose "No" and fix the line by hand.

## 2D (the Universal 2D template), checked in this version
- A project made from Universal 2D opens SampleScene with Main Camera (orthographic, Size 5, a dark blue background) and Global Light 2D. A window titled "2D URP Project" may open over the Editor: close it. Assets holds Scenes and Settings; InputSystem_Actions is in Assets/Settings, and InputSystem.actions.FindAction("Move") and FindAction("Jump") work as in the 3D project.
- In a project made from Universal 2D the project's input actions are NOT switched on when Play starts (in Universal 3D they are): every script that uses InputSystem.actions calls InputSystem.actions.Enable(); in Start before FindAction, or nothing moves. A picture in a 2D project imports with Sprite Mode "Multiple" (the sprite is then named Hero_0 and trimmed): set Sprite Mode to "Single" with Pixels Per Unit.
- GameObject > 2D Object: Sprites (Square, Circle, Capsule, Triangle, 9-Sliced, Hexagon Flat Top, Hexagon Point Top, Isometric Diamond), Physics (Dynamic Sprite, Static Sprite), Tilemap (Rectangular, Hexagonal Flat Top, Hexagonal Point Top, Isometric, Isometric Z as Y), Sprite Shape, Sprite Mask. These 2D menus exist only in a 2D project: the 3D project has no Sprites or Tilemap entries.
- GameObject > 2D Object > Tilemap > Rectangular adds a Grid with a child Tilemap (components: Tilemap, Tilemap Renderer). The palette is Window > 2D > Tile Palette. Assets > Create > 2D: Sprites (the same shapes), Tile Palette > Rectangular, Tiles > Rule Tile, Sprite Atlas.
- Component > Physics 2D: Rigidbody 2D, Box Collider 2D, Circle Collider 2D, Capsule Collider 2D, Polygon Collider 2D, Edge Collider 2D, Composite Collider 2D. Component > Tilemap: Tilemap Collider 2D.
- To merge a tilemap's colliders: add Composite Collider 2D to the Tilemap (this adds a Rigidbody 2D: set its Body Type to Static), then on Tilemap Collider 2D set "Composite Operation" to Merge. There is no "Used By Composite" checkbox in this version.
